fullPassage: Habits are part of our everyday lives and therefore, when we don't clean our teeth, eat breakfast, have our morning coffee or have biscuits in the afternoon, we feel unsettled and a little bit stressed. This feeling is unpleasant and we quickly learn that it can be avoided by carrying on with our habit. Therefore, not eating biscuits feels unusual, but this can all be made OK with a few biscuits. And the habit carries on as it becomes the solution to the problem created when trying to change it. It's a vicious circle. But it's the change in the habit which makes us feel stressed, not the absence of the actual behaviour. And if we start to realise that the feeling of stress or worry is just 'withdrawal' and will only be made worse in the longer term if we give in and use the habit to get rid of it, then we can start to break the habit itself.

습관을 끊으려 할 때 느끼는 스트레스에 굴복하면 습관이 더 쉽게 사라진다.

questions.passage: Habits are part of our everyday lives and therefore, when we don't clean our teeth, eat breakfast, have our morning coffee or have biscuits in the afternoon, we feel unsettled and a little bit stressed. This feeling is unpleasant and we quickly learn that it can be avoided by carrying on with our habit. Therefore, not eating biscuits feels unusual, but this can all be made OK with a few biscuits. And the habit carries on as it becomes the solution to the problem created when trying to change it. It's a vicious circle. But it's the change in the habit which makes us feel stressed, not the absence of the actual behaviour. And if we start to realise that the feeling of stress or worry is just 'withdrawal' and will only be made worse in the longer term if we give in and use the habit to get rid of it, then we can start to break the habit itself.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 본문과 정확히 일치하는 선지 찾기
det.analysis:
❌ ① 불일치: 변화 시 스트레스가 증가한다고 함. 줄어든다는 것은 반대
✅ ② 일치: 'the feeling of stress or worry is just withdrawal' — 스트레스/걱정이 금단 증상(withdrawal)이라고 직접 서술
❌ ③ 불일치: 'will only be made worse in the longer term if we give in' — 굴복하면 더 나빠짐. 완화가 아님
❌ ④ 불일치: 'Habits are part of our everyday lives' — 일상의 일부라고 함. 영향 없다는 것은 반대
det.tip: withdrawal = 금단 증상. 필자가 습관 중단 시 스트레스를 금단 증상에 비유하는 것이 핵심 주장

ch: 습관을 바꾸면 처음에는 스트레스가 줄어들고 점차 편안해진다.

습관에 굴복하면 장기적으로 금단 증상이 완화된다.
일상적 습관은 우리의 삶에 거의 영향을 미치지 않는다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① carries=이어가다(3인칭 단수 정상), ② created=만들어진(과거분사 정상), ③ which→what 오류(선행사 the change가 있으므로 관계대명사 which 필요), ④ worse=더 나쁜(비교급 정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① carries: 'the habit carries on' — 3인칭 단수 주어에 -s 정상
❌ ② created: 'the problem created when trying to change it' — 과거분사 후치수식 정상
✅ ③ what: 'the change in the habit what makes us feel stressed' — 선행사 the change가 있으므로 관계대명사 which가 맞음. what은 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사로 선행사와 함께 쓸 수 없음
❌ ④ worse: 'will only be made worse' — 비교급 형용사 보어 정상
det.tip: which vs what: 선행사 있으면 which/that, 선행사 없으면 what. the change(선행사) + which(관계대명사)
